controlled_change: Planned native decode-only packed-r2 option and 1072/1460 expert slots in a two-by-two comparison; fixed mixed artifact, residency, 12GiB maximum, schedules and sampling.
correctness: The standalone Q4 candidate and existing diagnostic kernels match hidden/final output bytes for 64 real expert/input cases, with BF16 and FP32 outputs and Metal validation. Native integration, full-model state parity and combined requests have not run.
decision_origin: authored interpretation; original report statuses retained
expected_effect: Evaluate the existing 20ms/token combined stage target without adding the separate operator and cache savings as a prediction.
hypothesis: Packed Q4 expert arithmetic can combine with one extra GiB of expert cache to reduce normal decode latency more than either component alone.
limitations: This is a new proposed combined experiment; neither prior individual gate result is relabeled as passing.
Operator GPU savings cannot be added to cache or request savings; overlaps must be measured.
Per-dispatch GPU counter intervals overlap and are instrumentation affected.
Four decode steps do not establish steady generation or 2K/4K acceptance.
No production default, precision, router or expert selection changed.
outcome: The resumed full-model four-step diagnostic completed in 93.57 seconds with matching tokens/reuse and clean sampled memory. Packed Q4 reduces isolated expert GPU duration by 43-47 percent, including a separate 128MiB-copy locality intervention. Both screens retain insufficient_benefit: their frequency projections are 13.57-14.44ms/token, below the individual 20ms gate. No request gain is established.
smallest_experiment: Implement the shape- and phase-limited native Q4 option, prove all-layer state/cancellation/failure parity, then run A B C D and D C B A normal conversations for reference/packed Q4 at 1072/1460 slots. Require measurable kernel benefit at both capacities and the combined request gate before five-pair confirmation.
